headline.technical: Nvidia's leadership change and a Treasury sell-off ahead of US inflation data weigh on sentiment; the S&P 500 closed -0.35% on 2026-11-12 while the Euro Stoxx 50 is 0.15% on 2026-11-13.
headline.layman: Nvidia's boss stepped down and bond prices are sliding before US inflation numbers. US stocks slipped a little; European stocks edged up.

global.title: Nvidia fallout and a Treasury sell-off set the tone

status.technical: WSJ reported stock futures fell as fallout from Nvidia's leadership change continued and longer-dated Treasurys sold off ahead of key US inflation data. The Financial Times said Treasuries are set for their worst week since 'liberation day'. US 10-year yield closed at 5.10 (1d 2.10%); VIX 18.36.
status.layman: WSJ said stock futures fell because of Nvidia's leadership change and because bond prices kept dropping before US inflation data. The Financial Times said it is the worst week for US government bonds since 'liberation day'.

consequence.technical: CNBC reported October inflation beat expectations at 0.4% for the month and that traders have strengthened Fed rate hike bets. If the new inflation data again run hot, then rate-hike expectations could firm further, per CNBC's framing.
consequence.layman: CNBC said October inflation came in higher than expected, at 0.4% for the month, and traders now bet more on Fed rate rises. If the next data is also hot, those bets could grow.

impact.technical: Bloomberg said inflation and a hawkish Fed are pushing yields higher, so the haven trade in Treasuries did not last. Bond holders are hit first; the notes give thinner evidence on other sectors beyond AI and chips.
impact.layman: Bloomberg said high inflation and a Fed that sounds tough are pushing bond yields up, so bonds were not a safe place for long. People holding bonds feel it first. Evidence on other groups is thin.

outlook.technical: After ordinary days, S&P 500 next day rose 54% of the time and next 5 days rose 59% of the time. These are historical base rates, not predictions.
outlook.layman: In the past, after ordinary days like this one, the S&P 500 was higher the next day 54% of the time and higher five days later 59% of the time. These are past patterns, not predictions.

status.technical: Dow Jones -0.36%, S&P 500 -0.35%, Nasdaq -0.39% and Russell 2000 -1.66% on 2026-11-12. Bloomberg said US stocks drifted ahead of the inflation test of Fed bets; Nvidia was -4.34% (1d) among the S&P 500's largest names.
status.layman: US stocks ended lower on 2026-11-12: S&P 500 -0.35%, Nasdaq -0.39%. Bloomberg said stocks drifted before the inflation test. Nvidia, one of the biggest US companies, fell -4.34%.

consequence.technical: WSJ said the AI trade faces two major tests next week: Nvidia's earnings and Anthropic's IPO. If either disappoints, then AI-linked shares could stay under pressure; the notes do not give results yet.
consequence.layman: WSJ said the AI trade has two big tests next week: Nvidia's earnings report and Anthropic's stock market debut. If those go badly, AI shares could stay under pressure. Nothing is known yet.

impact.technical: Bloomberg reported a graft scandal is eroding trust in Mexico's electoral authority, with nearly half of Mexicans having little or no confidence; the S&P/BMV IPC closed -0.27%. Evidence linking this to equities is thin.
impact.layman: Bloomberg said a corruption scandal has hurt Mexicans' trust in their election authority; nearly half have little or no confidence. The link to Mexican stocks is not shown, so evidence is thin.

status.layman: European shares were calm but are heading for their best week since June, said Investing.com. The Euro Stoxx 50 rose 0.15% and Germany's DAX is at its 52-week high.

consequence.layman: Bloomberg said the euro area is growing solidly, which lets the European Central Bank raise interest rates again to fight inflation. Its main rate is 2.65 %, up from 2.4. If it hikes again, borrowing gets pricier.

status.layman: Chinese stocks fell on 2026-11-13: Hang Seng -1.55% and Shenzhen -2.05%. The Financial Times said Chinese AI shares are being sold on fears of tougher limits on Nvidia chip sales. Japan's Nikkei rose 0.53%.

consequence.technical: SCMP reported SMIC sees an AI computing crunch until 2028 as Nvidia heat risks tighter chip curbs. If curbs tighten, then Chinese AI projects reliant on Nvidia could be hit; Investing.com cited $3 billion of such projects at risk.
consequence.layman: SCMP said China's chipmaker SMIC expects a shortage of AI computing power until 2028. If the US tightens chip limits, Chinese AI projects using Nvidia chips could suffer; Investing.com cited $3 billion at risk.

impact.layman: The biggest Hong Kong names all fell: Tencent -3.06%, Alibaba -3.46%, Meituan -3.19%. In India, a long rally paused with Nifty 50 at -0.61%.

status.layman: CNBC said Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday. That is shaking chip stocks, and Nvidia fell -4.34% in a day.

consequence.technical: Al Jazeera reported the Senate Banking Committee summoned Huang and Lutnick to testify. If the hearings or chip-sale scrutiny widen, then China-exposed AI names could stay volatile, per the FT's reporting on tougher-restriction fears.
consequence.layman: Al Jazeera said US senators want Huang and the Commerce Secretary to testify. If scrutiny grows, shares tied to Nvidia's China sales could stay jumpy.

impact.technical: WSJ said Nvidia's earnings next week are a major test for the AI trade; Singapore's Straits Times reported trading interest in Nvidia jumped up to 11 times at broking platforms. Evidence on wider effects is thin.
impact.layman: WSJ said Nvidia's report next week is a big test for AI shares. In Singapore, the Straits Times said interest in Nvidia jumped up to 11 times at some brokers.

status.technical: Financial Times: Treasuries set for worst week since 'liberation day'. CNBC: yields rose as traders strengthened Fed rate hike bets. US 10-year yield closed at 5.10 (5d 5.50%); Japan Bonds fell as the Treasury rout extended, Bloomberg said.
status.layman: US government bond prices are falling, which pushes yields up. CNBC said traders now expect the Fed to raise rates. The 10-year yield closed at 5.10.

consequence.technical: If inflation data confirm the October reading of 0.4% for the month (CNBC), then rate-hike bets could strengthen further; the CNBC piece says the Fed is bracing for another inflation fight.
consequence.layman: If new inflation data are also hot, like October's 0.4% for the month, traders may bet even more on rate rises, said CNBC.

impact.technical: Bloomberg said the Treasury haven trade did not last. The dollar index closed 103.25 (5d 0.93%) and EUR/USD closed 1.11; the notes give no further sector detail.
impact.layman: Bond buyers lost their safe-haven status for now. The US dollar index is at 103.25. The notes say little about other groups.

drivers.title: Oil prices easing as supply returns

status.technical: FT: global oil markets swing to surplus as Gulf shipments rebound. Brent closed 95.70 (1m -9.65%), WTI 88.23. WSJ said a fall in oil buoyed European stocks.
status.layman: The Financial Times said there is now more oil than needed as Gulf shipments return. Brent is 95.70, down -9.65% in a month.

consequence.technical: IEA analysts, per the FT, warn it will take months to rebuild stockpiles depleted by conflict. If supply keeps rebounding, then oil could stay lower; the notes do not forecast a level.
consequence.layman: IEA analysts told the FT it will take months to refill emergency oil stores drained by conflict. If supply keeps coming back, oil may stay cheaper.

impact.technical: Economic Times said the Indian rupee snapped a rising streak on a hawkish Fed and an oil rise; USD/INR closed 94.23. Europe benefited from the oil drop per WSJ.
impact.layman: Economic Times said the rupee weakened on oil and the Fed. European stocks got a lift from cheaper oil, said WSJ.

outlook.technical: Brent correlates with the Euro Stoxx 50 at -0.51 in the data (prior-day); base rates are not predictions.
outlook.layman: Past data show European stocks tend to do better when oil falls. This is a past pattern, not a prediction.

status.technical: CNBC and the FT reported a widespread Microsoft outage taking down Outlook, Teams and 365 services. Microsoft said it was not caused by malicious or cyber activity. Mint said it forced traders to use phones.
status.layman: A big Microsoft outage knocked out Outlook and Teams. Microsoft said it was not a cyber attack. Mint said traders had to use phones.

consequence.technical: The notes give no market-level consequence yet; SCMP reported Hong Kong banks' work was disrupted.
consequence.layman: The notes do not say what this means for prices. SCMP said it slowed work at Hong Kong banks.

impact.technical: Financial firms and government offices were affected, per Mint; the Straits Times said banks offered alternative contact channels. Evidence on market impact is thin.
impact.layman: Banks and government offices were slowed down. We have little evidence about price effects.

outlook.technical: No base rate in the data covers outages; evidence is thin.
outlook.layman: No past-pattern data covers outages, so there is nothing to say about what comes next.

consequence.layman: If inflation stays above the RBI's 6 per cent upper limit, a rate rise becomes more likely. Mint said company profits and foreign buying decide if the rally lasts.
